claim: Words may begin with stops, nasals, glides, or vowels, but not with underlying rhotics; no underlying lateral-initial words are listed either.
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Surface initial [l] is possible through positional neutralization with /d/; this is not analyzed as an underlying lateral-initial lexical contrast.

claim: Medial /l/ is contrastive, but word-initial /l/ neutralizes with /d/: /duwa/ 'boomerang' varies as [duwa] ~ [luwa], and Crowley therefore lists no words as underlyingly lateral-initial.
normalized_environment: LATERAL~STOP NEUTRALIZATION / WORD_INITIAL; /l/ contrast retained MEDIALLY
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The [luwa] surface variant shows that a surface lateral can occur word-initially even though the underlying /l/ contrast is neutralized there.

claim: Word-final position licenses only vowels, nasals, /j/, /l/, and /r/.
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The statement is a secondary summary of Crowley 1979 and does not specify whether every nasal or rhotic phoneme is equally represented in final position.

claim: Comparative forms support historical loss of an initial consonant in Yaygir, producing vowel-initial words where cognates retain an initial velar consonant.
exceptions_or_counterexamples: These examples establish a historical source for some onsetless initial words but do not imply that every present-day vowel-initial word derives from consonant loss.

claim: Crowley's grammar places synchronic phonotactics in §2.2 (p.369) and historical initial consonant deletion/lenition in §2.3.1 (p.371), providing the primary-source targets for direct verification of the secondary-source records.
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The accessible primary PDF was blocked during this run, so this record does not independently assert the detailed contents of §2.2 beyond its documented section title and pagination.
section: 2.2 Phonotactics; 2.3.1 Initial consonant deletion and lenition
